answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 41% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the attacker's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the hollow reward in the mirror ledger costs the operator directly, and the marble audit records each payout. A farm of 146 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
